predecessors.name: Mughal Empire
predecessors.text: the 28 and a half parganas about Indore granted by the Peshwa on 29 July 1732

successors.name: Madhya Bharat
successors.text: the Holkar districts of the 1931 state: Indore, Maheshwar, Khargone and the Nimar side, Mehidpur, Rampura and Bhanpura (24,605 km2 on the page; scattered)

ledger.x: 29 July 1732: the Peshwa grants Malhar Rao Holkar the Holkar state.
1767: Ahilyabai Holkar moves the capital from Indore to Maheshwar.

ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 24 December 1805: Holkar signs the Treaty of Rajghat.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 24 December 1805: Holkar gives up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 21 December 1817: the British beat Holkar at Mahidpur.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 6 January 1818: the Treaty of Mandeswar (Mandsaur) is signed; Holkar "accepted the British terms in totality" and the Holkar state became subsidiary to the British (Indore State page: British protectorate).
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 1818: the Holkars lose much of their territory.
ledger.cpn: British Empire in India (East India Company rule)

ledger.x: 3 November 1818: the capital returns from Maheshwar to Indore and the Indore Residency is established.
16 June 1948: Indore merges into Madhya Bharat.

wars.name: Battle of Poona
wars.outcome: Holkar beats the combined armies of the Peshwa and Scindia on 25 October 1802 (Diwali); Baji Rao II flees to the British and signs the Treaty of Bassein in December.

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War (Holkar phase)
wars.outcome: British hostilities from 6 April 1804; Holkar fails at Delhi and Bharatpur; the Treaty of Rajghat of 24 December 1805 returns his territory and takes Tonk, Rampura and Bundi.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War (Holkar phase)
wars.outcome: British victory at Mahidpur on 21 December 1817; Treaty of Mandeswar of 6 January 1818 makes the Holkar state subsidiary.

certainty.note: The pages give parganas, towns and districts but no boundaries; the pre-1818 extent is not described at all.

A British subsidiary state with a recorded area (24,605 km2 in 1931) of scattered districts; the detached portions are drawn by circles around the district towns, so the edge is sharp in law but approximate in the drawing.
